judged_text: The new Salesforce refresh path never routes through refreshOAuthTokens, so the APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED / CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT gating that every other app in this diff honors is silently unchecked here, while parseRefreshTokenResponse still switches to the stripping minimum schema when sharing is on. A self-hoster running credential sync still must hold real Salesforce client secrets and per-user refresh tokens inside Cal.com (sync is unimplemented for Salesforce), and in sharing mode the persisted key is stripped to {access_token, refresh_token} - losing instance_url, id and signature - so subsequent jsforce connections target the wrong host and Salesforce operations fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow directly `fetch`es Salesforce’s token endpoint and never calls the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper that other integrations were updated to use, so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set the credential-sync pathway is not honored for Salesforce at all. At the same time it *does* call `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which conditionally switches to the “minimum” token schema under those same env conditions, and then persists `key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }`. That means in credential-sharing mode the updated stored credential can lose fields required by the normal Salesforce token shape (e.g., `instance_url`, `id`, `signature`) because the minimum schema is used instead of `salesforceTokenSchema`, creating a real risk of broken subsequent Salesforce usage from the persisted credential.
